name: ISO 26262 functional safety
copyrightNotice: ISO standard text is copyrighted and is not bundled. Obtain the official standard for authoritative requirements.
disclaimer: This original readiness profile is not the ISO standard, legal advice, certification, or a determination of conformity. Evidence matches require qualified functional-safety review.

controls.title: Safety plan and responsibilities
controls.objective: Maintain an approved safety plan, lifecycle responsibilities, independence, and escalation routes.

controls.title: Item definition and hazard analysis
controls.objective: Define the item and retain reviewable hazard analysis and risk classification evidence.

controls.title: Safety goals and traceable requirements
controls.objective: Trace safety goals through functional, technical, hardware, and software requirements.

controls.title: Verification and validation evidence
controls.objective: Retain review, test, integration, validation, and coverage evidence tied to safety requirements.

controls.title: Configuration and change control
controls.objective: Control baselines, safety-impacting changes, problem resolution, and tool confidence evidence.

controls.title: Independent confirmation and safety case
controls.objective: Record independent reviews, audits, assessments, and the integrated safety case.

name: ISO/SAE 21434 automotive cybersecurity
copyrightNotice: ISO/SAE standard text is copyrighted and is not bundled. Obtain the official standard for authoritative requirements.
disclaimer: This original readiness profile is not the ISO/SAE standard, legal advice, certification, or a determination of conformity. Evidence matches require qualified cybersecurity review.

controls.title: Cybersecurity governance
controls.objective: Define policy, responsibilities, competence, quality management, and cybersecurity planning.

controls.title: Assets, threats, and risk analysis
controls.objective: Maintain item definition, asset inventory, threat scenarios, attack paths, risk decisions, and cybersecurity goals.

controls.title: Secure development and verification
controls.objective: Retain secure design, implementation, review, testing, and vulnerability analysis evidence.

controls.title: Supplier and interface controls
controls.objective: Document cybersecurity interfaces, supplier expectations, dependencies, and software inventory.

controls.title: Monitoring, incident, and update lifecycle
controls.objective: Operate vulnerability monitoring, incident response, field action, and secure update processes.

controls.title: Cybersecurity case and release judgment
controls.objective: Integrate claims, evidence, residual risk acceptance, and release approval into a reviewable cybersecurity case.

name: UNECE Regulation No. 155
copyrightNotice: Use the official UNECE regulation and applicable type-approval guidance as the authoritative source.
disclaimer: This readiness profile is not type approval, legal advice, certification, or a determination of regulatory conformity. Applicability and evidence require competent legal and type-approval review.

controls.title: Cybersecurity management system
controls.objective: Maintain governed, auditable cybersecurity processes across development, production, and post-production.

controls.title: Vehicle threats, risks, and mitigations
controls.objective: Identify vehicle threats and attack paths, assess risks, select mitigations, and verify effectiveness.

controls.title: Security testing and evidence
controls.objective: Retain vehicle and component testing evidence for implemented cybersecurity measures.

controls.title: Detection, monitoring, and incident response
controls.objective: Monitor relevant threats and vulnerabilities and maintain response, reporting, and remediation processes.

controls.title: Supplier cybersecurity dependencies
controls.objective: Manage supplier, service-provider, and component cybersecurity dependencies with traceable agreements.

controls.title: Approval scope and representative evidence
controls.objective: Confirm vehicle-type scope, authority expectations, declarations, and representative evidence through qualified review.

name: UNECE Regulation No. 156
copyrightNotice: Use the official UNECE regulation and applicable type-approval guidance as the authoritative source.
disclaimer: This readiness profile is not type approval, legal advice, certification, or a determination of regulatory conformity. Applicability and evidence require competent legal and type-approval review.

controls.title: Software update management system
controls.objective: Govern software update responsibilities, processes, records, and continual improvement.

controls.title: Vehicle software inventory and versions
controls.objective: Maintain traceable software, configuration, dependency, vehicle-type, and version information.

controls.title: Update authenticity and integrity
controls.objective: Protect update packages, delivery, authorization, installation, and associated cryptographic keys.

controls.title: Compatibility, recovery, and safe installation
controls.objective: Assess compatibility, prerequisites, safe state, recovery, rollback, and user information before release.

controls.title: Release approval and audit trail
controls.objective: Retain approvals, distribution records, installation outcomes, failures, and field monitoring evidence.

controls.title: Approval scope and authority evidence
controls.objective: Confirm applicable vehicle-type and update scope with the relevant approval authority.

name: EU General Data Protection Regulation
jurisdiction: European Union and applicable extraterritorial processing
copyrightNotice: Use EUR-Lex and competent supervisory-authority guidance as authoritative legal sources.
disclaimer: This technical readiness profile is not legal advice and does not determine GDPR applicability or compliance. Legal basis, proportionality, risk, and accountability require qualified privacy review.

controls.title: Processing inventory and ownership
controls.objective: Document processing activities, data categories, purposes, systems, recipients, owners, and transfers.

controls.title: Purpose, lawful basis, notices, and consent
controls.objective: Document purpose limitation, lawful bases, transparent notices, and consent where relied upon.

controls.title: Rights request operations
controls.objective: Operate authenticated, timely access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, and objection workflows.

controls.title: Minimization, privacy engineering, and risk assessment
controls.objective: Apply minimization and privacy by design and perform DPIAs where processing risk requires them.

controls.title: Security, retention, deletion, and incidents
controls.objective: Protect personal data, test safeguards, enforce retention/deletion, and operate breach assessment and notification.

controls.title: Processor and transfer governance
controls.objective: Inventory processors, execute required terms, assess international transfers, and oversee safeguards.

controls.title: Applicability, roles, and supervisory obligations
controls.objective: Have qualified reviewers confirm territorial/material scope, controller/processor roles, DPO duties, and authority obligations.

name: California CCPA/CPRA readiness
copyrightNotice: Use current California statutes, regulations, agency guidance, and counsel as authoritative sources.
disclaimer: This technical readiness profile is not legal advice and does not determine CCPA/CPRA applicability or compliance. Thresholds, exceptions, notices, and operational duties require qualified legal review.

controls.title: Personal information inventory and purpose controls
controls.objective: Inventory personal and sensitive personal information, sources, purposes, disclosures, sales, and sharing.

controls.title: Notices and privacy disclosures
controls.objective: Maintain notices at collection and a complete, accessible privacy policy aligned with actual processing.

controls.title: Consumer rights operations
controls.objective: Operate verifiable request intake and fulfillment for access, correction, deletion, portability, and related rights.

controls.title: Choice signals and sensitive information
controls.objective: Honor applicable opt-out, preference, and limit-use signals, including documented Global Privacy Control handling.

controls.title: Third-party contracts and oversight
controls.objective: Classify recipients and maintain required contractual restrictions, due diligence, and monitoring.

controls.title: Security, risk assessments, audits, and ADMT
controls.objective: Maintain reasonable security and assess current statutory and regulatory duties for risk assessments, cybersecurity audits, and automated decisionmaking technology.

controls.title: Thresholds, roles, minors, and exceptions
controls.objective: Have qualified counsel confirm business thresholds, roles, exceptions, minors' data duties, and enforcement exposure.

name: NIST Privacy Framework
copyrightNotice: This profile is an original high-level mapping. Use NIST's official publication for framework outcomes and implementation guidance.
disclaimer: This starter profile does not reproduce the full NIST Privacy Framework and is not certification, legal advice, or proof that privacy risk is acceptable. Tailoring and stakeholder review are required.

controls.title: Data processing understanding
controls.objective: Understand systems, products, services, data actions, individuals, roles, and privacy risks.

controls.title: Privacy governance
controls.objective: Establish policies, roles, risk tolerance, legal context, training, and oversight.

controls.title: Granular processing control
controls.objective: Enable appropriate policies, preferences, permissions, minimization, deletion, and individual participation.

controls.title: Transparency and data-processing communication
controls.objective: Communicate processing practices, purposes, risks, choices, and responsibilities to individuals and partners.

controls.title: Data safeguards
controls.objective: Apply access, data, platform, resilience, maintenance, and security controls proportionate to privacy risk.

controls.title: Tailored target profile and improvement plan
controls.objective: Document current and target profiles, prioritization, resource decisions, and improvement ownership.

name: ISO/IEC 27001 information security management
copyrightNotice: ISO standard text is copyrighted and is not bundled. Obtain the official standard for authoritative requirements and controls.
disclaimer: This original readiness profile is not the ISO standard, legal advice, accreditation, certification, or a determination of conformity. ISMS scope and effectiveness require competent independent review.

controls.title: Context, interested parties, and scope
controls.objective: Define organizational context, interested parties, interfaces, dependencies, and a defensible ISMS scope.

controls.title: Policy, roles, competence, and communication
controls.objective: Establish leadership commitment, policy, roles, resources, competence, awareness, communication, and document control.

controls.title: Risk assessment and treatment
controls.objective: Operate repeatable information-security risk assessment, treatment, acceptance, objectives, and change planning.

controls.title: Control applicability and implementation evidence
controls.objective: Maintain a versioned Statement of Applicability with reasons, owners, implementation state, and linked evidence.

controls.title: Monitoring, internal audit, and management review
controls.objective: Measure ISMS performance and retain internal audit, management review, findings, and corrective-action evidence.

controls.title: Technical security verification
controls.objective: Link risk treatment and applicable controls to current source, dependency, binary, and verification evidence.

controls.title: Independent audit and certification decisions
controls.objective: Keep certification scope, audit competence, nonconformity decisions, and accreditation claims under authorized independent control.

name: OWASP Top 10 Web Application Security Risks
copyrightNotice: Category titles and descriptions here are original paraphrases. The OWASP Top 10 is published under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0; consult the official page for the authoritative list.
disclaimer: This readiness profile is not the OWASP Top 10 document, an audit, a penetration test, or a determination that an application is secure. Category evidence matches require qualified application-security review.

controls.title: Broken access control
controls.objective: Deny-by-default authorization on server side, with access-control tests and no trusted client-side enforcement.

controls.title: Cryptographic failures
controls.objective: Classify and protect data in transit and at rest with current algorithms, key management, and no legacy protocols.

controls.title: Injection
controls.objective: Keep untrusted input out of interpreters through parameterized interfaces and server-side validation.

controls.title: Insecure design
controls.objective: Threat-model the system and retain secure design patterns, trust boundaries, and abuse-case evidence.

controls.title: Security misconfiguration
controls.objective: Harden environments by default with reviewable, differential configuration and no unused features or default accounts.

controls.title: Vulnerable and outdated components
controls.objective: Inventory components with versions, track advisories, and remove or patch unsupported dependencies.

controls.title: Identification and authentication failures
controls.objective: Confirm identities with hardened session management, credential storage, rotation, and attack resistance.

controls.title: Software and data integrity failures
controls.objective: Verify integrity of updates, dependencies, and pipelines with signatures, secure deserialization, and trusted repositories.

controls.title: Security logging and monitoring failures
controls.objective: Log security-relevant events with retention and alerting, protected against injection and tampering.

controls.title: Server-side request forgery
controls.objective: Validate redirects and fetches against allow-lists, with egress separation for user-influenced requests.

name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (common criteria)
domain: System security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy
copyrightNotice: Criteria descriptions here are original paraphrases. The Trust Services Criteria are copyrighted by the American Institute of CPAs; licensed guidance must be obtained for authoritative criteria.
disclaimer: This readiness profile is not a SOC 2 report, an audit, an attestation, or a determination of control effectiveness. Readiness evidence requires review by a qualified independent CPA.

controls.title: Control environment
controls.objective: Demonstrate integrity, board oversight, accountability, competence, and HR structures supporting the system.

controls.title: Communication and information
controls.objective: Communicate objectives, responsibilities, and quality information internally, externally, and over time.

controls.title: Risk assessment
controls.objective: Identify, analyze, and manage threats, misstatements, and fraud risks to objectives, including change-driven risk.

controls.title: Monitoring activities
controls.objective: Ongoing and separate evaluations of control performance, with communicator-recipient defect remediation.

controls.title: Control activities
controls.objective: Select and deploy risk-mitigating manual and automated activities with segregation and periodic reevaluation.

controls.title: Logical and physical access
controls.objective: Restrict logical and physical access to authorized users, assets, and data, with provisioning, transfer, and removal controls.

controls.title: System operations
controls.objective: Detect, analyze, and respond to security events and incidents with recovery and continuity management.

controls.title: Change management
controls.objective: Authorize, test, approve, and track changes to infrastructure, software, and procedures with rollback.

controls.title: Risk mitigation (vendors and business)
controls.objective: Identify vendor and business-continuity risk, select mitigating controls, and monitor vendor performance.

controls.title: Independent CPA examination
controls.objective: Engage a qualified independent CPA to examine controls and issue the report; readiness here is not attestation.
